story: The NASA rover Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021, to explore an ancient lake and river delta. Equipped with a complex sample-caching system and terrain-relative navigation, the car-sized, nuclear-powered rover aims to search for signs of past microbial life. Alongside collecting rock and regolith samples, it carries seven primary instruments like SHERLOC and PIXL, two audio microphones, and the experimental helicopter Ingenuity, which performed the first powered flight on another planet. It also successfully tested oxygen production from the Martian atmosphere using MOXIE.
angle: Perseverance deployed Ingenuity, achieving the first powered and controlled flight on another planet.

claims.claim: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021.
The rover is powered by a multi-mission radioisotope thermoelectric generator (MMRTG) using plutonium-238 oxide.
Ingenuity performed the first powered and controlled flight on another planet.
Jezero Crater is approximately 28 to 30 miles wide.
Terrain Relative Navigation (TRN) allowed the rover to autonomously guide itself to a safer landing.
The MOXIE experiment successfully produced oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere.
Perseverance carries 43 sample tubes for caching rocks and regolith.
Over 10.9 million names were submitted to the 'Send Your Name to Mars' campaign and etched onto silicon chips on the rover.
The rover has a mass of approximately 1,025 to 1,026 kilograms (around 2,260 pounds).
The mission was launched on July 30, 2020, aboard an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral.
Perseverance carries seven primary scientific instruments.
